messages:
oncall-bot: Paging SRE oncall: detected p99 tail above SLO for canary: model v5-quant at 2501234400
alex_chung: saw it too. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s on canary shards, p99 ~3.4s. Rolling canary started ~2501234300.
priya.k: where's traffic weight? did we ramp past 10%?
marco: traffic was at 25% at 2501234350 due to automated ramp rule (ramp-to-25-after-5m).
li-ops: streaming stalls reported — clients saw stalled event chunks, websocket heartbeats fine but no tokens. logs show "kv_cache_miss" spike and repeated `AcquireKVLock timeout` on encoder nodes.
alex_chung: that's consistent with quantized kernel path thrashing. We saw similar with v3-quant in staging.
priya.k: severity? what's customer impact? any 5xxs or just latency?
support-bot: Incoming alerts: 0.8% of requests returned 504/timeout, streaming session drop rate up to 3.2% for canary region eu-west-1.
kate_support: we have two Enterprise customers reporting degraded sessions. CS notified; they're collecting examples.
marco: I'm going to pause the canary ramp and flip a traffic split to fallback model variant (v5-fp16) for canary traffic. Need a rollback if that doesn't help.
li-ops: command to shift traffic:
```
redwoodctl rollout traffic-shift --deployment canary-v5 --to model-v5-fp16 --percent 25
```
marco: executing now.
deploy-bot: started traffic-shift job 87654 at 2501234601
alex_chung: also enabling prefix KV caching fallback for canary pods to reduce KV_lock churn:
```
PATCH /api/v1/configs/canary-v5
{ "kv_cache": { "mode": "aggressive_fallback" } }
```
li-ops: patch applied, service config reloaded. logs show kv errors dropping but tail still high.
priya.k: @marco if shift doesn't improve in 3m, rollback full canary -> previous stable v4.
marco: agreed. initiating progressive rollback plan.
marco: initiating rollback command:
```
redwoodctl deploy rollback --deployment canary-v5 --to model-v4-stable --force
```
deploy-bot: rollback job queued 87655
sre-manager: pinging infra team to check kernel scheduling and GPU mem pressure; could be kernel allocator regression under quantized kernels.
infra-bot: Observed NV_MEM_UTIL at 87% on encoder nodes; intermittent kernel preemption spikes.
li-ops: log extract:
```
[2501234670] encoder-3 | ERROR AcquireKVLock timeout after 50ms; queue_len=12
[2501234672] encoder-3 | WARN quant_kernel: fallback to slow path
```
alex_chung: fallback to slow path explains p99 but not initial kv_lock storm — maybe a contention bug in quant cache eviction.
kate_support: CS wants ETA to tell customers.
priya.k: temporary ETA: 15-25m. If rollback completes and p99 drops under 500ms we'll update earlier.
marco: rollback job started, deploy-bot reports progress: 30% -> 60% -> 100%
deploy-bot: rollback job 87655 completed at 2501234799; all canary replicas now model-v4-stable
oncall-bot: post-rollback check: p95 recovered to ~140ms, p99 to ~420ms in 120s window
alex_chung: streaming stall rate down to 0.4%, kv_lock logs subsided. Good.
li-ops: creating follow-up issue: #INC-2501 "v5-quant: kv cache eviction contention leading to tail latency" and attaching logs and flame graphs.
priya.k: SLO breach window documented. Need RCA runbook item: slow quant kernel fallback detection + safe ramp rule (cap ramp at 10% and require p99 < 300ms for 10m before >10%).
sre-manager: agree. Also add automated canary-health gating that checks KV_LOCK_RATE and STREAM_DROP_RATE before ramp.
kate_support: messaging drafted for impacted customers, awaiting final metrics. I'll post update in ~30m.
alex_chung: handoff to oncall for next 2h: monitoring for regression, follow-up triage tomorrow with ML infra + runtime team to root cause quant kernel interaction.
li-ops: adding runbook snippet to incident ticket and scheduling postmortem.
marco: thumbs up. closing live mitigation thread. :thumbsup: 
support-bot: Incident ticket INC-2501 created and linked to runbook.
oncall-bot: Handoff: next-oncall @sre-night. Please acknowledge and monitor until 2521234567.
sre-night: acknowledged. monitoring dashboards up and alerts suppressed for noise thresholds.
priya.k: thanks everyone. Postmortem invite to relevant folks in #postmortems.
